Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for a HIPAA-adjacent proof-of-concept and have two gating items from procurement + security: a clear contractual "no learning / no model improvement" commitment tied to our customer prompts, and operational evidence that processing and any subprocessors can be restricted to EU-only infrastructure (ideally single-tenant or VPC).

Specifically we need:
- A clean redline of your DPA showing explicit no-training/no-model-improvement language.
- Current subprocessor inventory and confirmation of their locations + any onshore processing options.
- An operational evidence pack: audit logs or examples showing SFTP/API export capabilities, KMS-onshore key control, and a sample monthly attestation we can pass to our auditors.

SOC 2 + IL/ISO proof is helpful but not sufficient alone — our auditors want an outline we can follow to verify you are not ingesting our prompts into model training. We have a tight approval window and our procurement target is to have answers by Apr 5.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can (1) commit contractually to no-training for our tenant, (2) provide an evidence package within 7 business days, and (3) if not, what the operational mitigation (e.g., Dedicated/Private deployment) looks like?

Best,

Olga — forwarding my notes inline against Priya's asks so you can pull the language into a redline.

> "A clean redline of your DPA showing explicit no-training/no-model-improvement language."
- Proposed contract language (short form): "Provider will not use Customer Prompt Data to improve, train, or update any machine learning model weights or training datasets. Provider may use aggregate telemetry that cannot be associated with Customer or an identified individual for service quality monitoring only."
- Consider adding a carveout for "synthetic telemetry" used for internal performance tuning — if customer wants zero risk, we should offer Private deployment and explicit exclusion of those telemetry paths.

> "Current subprocessor inventory and confirmation of their locations + any onshore processing options."
- We can produce an inventory snapshot PDF. For onshore processing: we can offer Dedicated capacity in EU or Private (customer-managed VPC) to keep processing within EU. KMS-in-customer-control is recommended for highest assurance.

> "Operational evidence pack (SFTP/API export, KMS control, monthly attestation)."
- We can generate: subprocessor inventory PDF, sample sftp export audit log (redacted), key rotation/KMS configuration export, and a templated monthly attestation signed by our security ops person. Allow 5 business days to assemble if infra team prioritizes.

Operational constraints (Dev, please confirm):
- No-training toggle is implemented at request-routing layer; for strict non-learning we must ensure KV caching does not backfill training datasets. On Redwood Hosted we have telemetry that could be used for aggregate monitoring; Dedicated/Private is the safe path for absolute prohibition.
- There may be a 2–3 week lead time to provision Dedicated EU capacity depending on current cluster utilization; Private deployments are on a separate provisioning track (~3–4 weeks).

If Procurement needs a signed statement vs. auditor-signed evidence, we can provide both: an ops attestation and a SOC/ISO excerpt.
